caller_persona.name: Derek Chen
caller_persona.mood: irritated; he has already lost an hour

opening_line: Yeah, hi. I can't get into my laptop at all now. It was working fine earlier this week, I tried a few times this morning and now it's just dead to me. Can you just fix it from your end?
hidden_root_cause: Derek changed his password on Monday. His old personal Android phone, which sits in a drawer at home still powered on, still has his office email account set up with the old password and keeps retrying in the background. Every retry counts as a failed sign-in, so his directory account keeps getting locked out. The sign-in screen shows 'The referenced account is currently locked out and may not be logged on to.' Unlocking the account in Active Directory needs admin rights.
correct_fix_steps: Ask for the exact message on the sign-in screen (the account is locked out).
Ask whether he changed his password recently (on Monday).
Ask which other devices have his work email or work account set up, and find the old Android phone that still has the old password.
Have him remove the work email account from the old phone, or turn the phone off, so it stops retrying.
Escalate to an admin to unlock the account, noting that the old phone caused the lockouts so it won't lock again.
red_herrings: Derek thinks someone is trying to hack his account.
The office Wi-Fi was slow when he arrived this morning.
His laptop's keyboard has a sticky 'e' key.
success_criteria: Agent gets the exact lockout message.
Agent links the lockouts to the recent password change and another device still using the old password.
Agent has the caller remove the account from, or power off, the old phone.
Agent escalates the unlock to an admin instead of attempting it.
Agent never asks for the old or new password.
Ticket is escalated and the escalation reason mentions the account unlock and the stale device.
